# Documentation for `graph-execution manager`, the generated password and sandboxes on macOS and Windows

## What to build

Documentation only: no source code changes. The earlier tasks of this run made graph-manager part of the `graph-execution` npm package. This task updates the READMEs, TESTING.md, the changelog and the project wiki so they describe what now exists. Read the spec `docs/prd/npm-manager.md` first: its Decisions table and Requirements are the source for every statement. Before writing a statement about behaviour, check it in the code (paths below); where the code differs from the spec, document the code and add the difference to the wiki page's "Known follow-ups".

What the earlier tasks delivered (all in the codebase now):

- `packages/graph-execution/scripts/bundle-manager.mjs` and the script `bundle:manager`: copy `apps/graph-manager/dist` into `packages/graph-execution/dist/manager`. The root `npm run build` builds the engine, the manager, then bundles. The engine's `dependencies` now include `fastify`, `@fastify/cookie`, `@fastify/static`, `@fastify/websocket` and `node-pty`.
- The subcommand `graph-execution manager` (`packages/graph-execution/src/cli.ts`, `packages/graph-execution/src/manager/`) with `--port`, `--host`, `--data-dir`, `--workspaces-dir`, `--no-open`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/password.ts`: without `GM_PASSWORD` a password is generated once, saved in `<dataDir>/password` (mode 600) and printed at startup as `Password: <password> (saved in <file>)`; with `GM_PASSWORD` the line is `Password: from GM_PASSWORD`.
- `apps/graph-manager/Dockerfile` starts `node /app/packages/graph-execution/dist/cli.js manager --no-open`.
- Windows `.cmd` shims in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts` (`graph-execution.cmd`, `graph-manager-mcp.cmd`).
- `defaultDockerSocket` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/config.ts` (order: `GM_DOCKER_SOCKET`, `DOCKER_HOST` when `unix://` or `npipe://`, `//./pipe/docker_engine` on Windows, else the first existing of `/var/run/docker.sock`, `~/.docker/run/docker.sock`, `~/.docker/desktop/docker.sock`), and the "Windows containers" reason in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-paths.ts`: on Windows a sandbox mounts the workspace at `/workspaces/<rel>`, runs as `1000:1000`, and gets `safe.directory=*`, `core.filemode=false` and the host's `core.autocrlf` through `GIT_CONFIG_*` variables.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `docs/prd/npm-manager.md` — the spec; the wiki decision table is derived from its Decisions table.
- `README.md` (root; section `## graph-manager` at about line 12, `## Development` at about line 24) — add the npm way first.
- `packages/graph-execution/README.md` (`## Requirements` ~line 43, `## Installation` ~line 65, `## Contents` ~line 37, `### Releasing` ~line 642) — this file ships in the npm package and is rendered by `graph-execution readme`; it needs a `## graph-manager` section and a line in Contents.
- `apps/graph-manager/README.md` — `## Quick start` (~line 13, Docker only today), `## Configuration` table (~lines 41–61), `## Sandboxed runs` (~lines 78–195; line ~104 "Outside Docker", lines ~188–195 "Not supported"), `## Local development` (~line 254), `## Limitations` (~line 301; line ~305 says the MCP shim is not written on Windows).
- `TESTING.md` — section `## graph-manager` (~line 126). It says "Without `GM_PASSWORD` the server exits 1 and prints `GM_PASSWORD is required`", which is no longer true.
- `docs/wiki/index.md`, `docs/wiki/features/graph-manager.md`, `docs/wiki/features/sandboxes.md`, and `docs/wiki/features/sandboxes.md` as the model for a feature page (Summary, Decisions table with a ticket column, follow-ups, code references).
- `packages/graph-execution/CHANGELOG.md` — format of an entry (`## <version> (<date>)`, `### Added`, `### Fixed`).
- `CLAUDE.md` — step 5 uses `npm run build -w graph-execution` and `node packages/graph-execution/dist/cli.js`; leave it unless a command in it no longer works.
- The code named in "What to build", to confirm flags, messages and file names.

## Patterns to follow

**Writing style of this repo's docs:** plain, short sentences; commands in fenced `bash` blocks; settings in tables; no marketing words. Example from `apps/graph-manager/README.md`:

```markdown
- When Docker isn't reachable, **Run in sandbox** is disabled with the reason, and `--sandbox` exits 2.
```

**Wiki decision table** (from `docs/wiki/features/sandboxes.md`):

```markdown
| Decision | Why | Ticket |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The sandbox is an option per run, off by default. | The user asked for it. | KAN-88 |
```

There is no Jira ticket for this change: write `npm-manager` in the Ticket column.

**Tests that read docs:** search for tests that assert README content before editing (`grep -rn "README" packages/graph-execution/src --include=*.test.ts apps/graph-manager/src --include=*.test.ts`). `packages/graph-execution/scripts/render-readme.mjs` renders the package README to `dist/README.html` at build; keep the Markdown valid (balanced code fences, tables with a header row).

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: a new section `## graph-manager` after the Usage sections (and a line in `## Contents`). Content: what graph-manager is in two sentences; `npm install -g graph-execution` then `graph-execution manager`; the two startup lines with an example password; the five flags in a table with their `GM_*` equivalents and defaults (port 7420, host 127.0.0.1, data dir `~/.graph-manager`, workspaces dir `~/graph-manager-workspaces`); where the password is stored and that `GM_PASSWORD` overrides it; that the manager installs the bundled skills into `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` at startup; a link to `apps/graph-manager/README.md` on GitHub (`https://github.com/romm0109/graph-execution/tree/main/apps/graph-manager`) for sandboxes, Docker and configuration.
- **IMPLEMENT**: in `## Requirements`, a note: the package depends on `node-pty` (used by graph-manager's terminals); on macOS and Windows it installs a prebuilt binary, on Linux `npm install` compiles it and needs Python 3, make and a C++ compiler (for example `build-essential` on Debian/Ubuntu).
- **IMPLEMENT**: in `### Releasing`, say that `prepublishOnly` builds the manager and bundles it, so publishing must run from a full checkout of the monorepo.
- **GOTCHA**: confirm the Linux statement by looking at `node_modules/node-pty/prebuilds` (which platforms have prebuilds); write what you find.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build -w graph-execution` (renders the README).

### UPDATE `README.md` (root)

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `## graph-manager`, lead with the npm commands, then keep the Docker way. In `## Development`, state that `npm run build` at the root builds the engine, the manager and the bundle.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `## Quick start` gets two subsections: "From npm" (`npm install -g graph-execution`, `graph-execution manager`, the password line) first, then "With Docker" (the existing text).
- **IMPLEMENT**: Configuration table: `GM_PASSWORD` is now optional (generated and saved in `<dataDir>/password` when unset); `GM_DOCKER_SOCKET` row describes the discovery order and `DOCKER_HOST`; add the flag for each variable that has one.
- **IMPLEMENT**: in `## Sandboxed runs`, a platform table with the columns Platform, Docker endpoint, Workspace path in the sandbox, Container user, How it was checked. Rows: Linux (`/var/run/docker.sock`; same path; workspace owner; automated tests and a real run), macOS with Docker Desktop (`/var/run/docker.sock` or `~/.docker/run/docker.sock`; same path; workspace owner; unit tests and CI only, not run against a real Docker Desktop), Windows with Docker Desktop in Linux-containers mode (`//./pipe/docker_engine`; `/workspaces/<rel>`; `1000:1000`; unit tests and CI only, not run against a real Docker Desktop). Below it: the Windows notes (git settings passed in, Windows containers are refused with the reason text, the workspaces folder must be on a drive Docker Desktop can share) and the macOS note (the workspaces folder must be under a folder Docker Desktop shares; `/Users` is shared by default).
- **IMPLEMENT**: remove the "Docker Desktop on macOS when graph-manager itself runs outside Docker" entry from "Not supported" and add: Windows containers, a remote Docker daemon (`tcp://`, `ssh://`), Podman. Remove the Windows shim limitation in `## Limitations`; if a Windows limitation remains in the code (check `process.platform === "win32"` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server`), document that one instead.
- **IMPLEMENT**: `## Local development`: `npm run build` at the root, then `node packages/graph-execution/dist/cli.js manager`, or `npm start -w graph-manager` as before.

### UPDATE `TESTING.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in `## graph-manager`, replace the "Without `GM_PASSWORD` the server exits 1" bullet with the new behaviour (generated password, the two output lines, the file), and add how to test the npm-installed manager: `npm run build` at the root, `npm pack -w graph-execution --pack-destination <tmp>`, `npm install <tarball>` in an empty temp folder, then `<tmp>/node_modules/.bin/graph-execution manager --no-open --port 0 --data-dir … --workspaces-dir …`. Keep the existing start command (`node apps/graph-manager/dist/server/main.js` with `GM_PASSWORD=pw`): it still works.

### CREATE `docs/wiki/features/npm-manager.md` and UPDATE `docs/wiki/index.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: sections Summary, Decisions (the spec's table plus the Ticket column), Known follow-ups, Code references. Follow-ups to list: sandboxes on macOS and Windows have not been run against a real Docker Desktop; `node-pty` is a hard dependency, so the engine's install needs build tools on Linux; no publish workflow in CI; `tcp://`/`ssh://` Docker hosts are ignored; plus anything you found that differs from the spec. Code references: the files listed in "What to build".
- **IMPLEMENT**: add the line `- [graph-manager from npm: graph-execution manager, generated password, sandboxes on macOS and Windows](features/npm-manager.md)` at the end of the Features list in `docs/wiki/index.md`.
- **IMPLEMENT**: in `docs/wiki/features/graph-manager.md` and `docs/wiki/features/sandboxes.md`, add one line under the Summary: "Since npm-manager, graph-manager also ships in the npm package and sandboxes also run on macOS and Windows: see [npm-manager](npm-manager.md)."

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/CHANGELOG.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: a new section at the top, `## Unreleased`, with `### Added`: `graph-execution manager` starts graph-manager from the npm package; a generated password when `GM_PASSWORD` is unset; Docker endpoint discovery (`DOCKER_HOST`, Docker Desktop sockets, the Windows named pipe); sandboxes on Windows with Docker Desktop; `.cmd` shims for graph-manager's terminals on Windows. And `### Changed`: the package now depends on fastify and node-pty. Do not change the version in any `package.json`.

### Limits to document (found while planning; check each in the code first)

- Windows sandboxes: the run's `state.json` and git worktree records hold `/workspaces/<rel>/…` paths, so the run page shows container paths; a `git worktree prune` on the host (also one from a non-sandboxed run in the same workspace) drops the worktree records of a paused sandboxed run. Put both under the Windows notes and in the wiki follow-ups.
- Windows terminals: after Ctrl+C in a `.cmd` shim, `cmd.exe` asks `Terminate batch job (Y/N)?`; an install or data path with non-ASCII characters may not work in a `.cmd` file. Qwen's committed `.qwen/settings.json` keeps the bare `graph-manager-mcp` name on every platform. Also remove the Windows limitation line in `docs/wiki/features/agent-tools.md` (about line 36) if the code no longer has it.
- macOS sandboxes: a provider login is copied from files under the home folder (`LOGIN_FILES` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts`). Where a CLI keeps its login in the macOS Keychain instead of a file, a sandboxed run needs the provider's API key or token variable (`LOGIN_KEYS` in the same file). Say this in the macOS note without claiming which CLIs do so.
- The fake Docker daemon (`apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs`) has a `--os-type` flag: add it to TESTING.md where the fake Docker is described, if it exists in the code.
- The engine's sandbox tools copy leaves out `dist/manager` and the manager-only dependencies (`apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-tools.ts`): one line in the wiki decisions.
- `GRAPH_EXECUTION_NO_OPEN=1` stops `graph-execution manager` from opening the browser: list it with `--no-open`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/graph-execution/README.md` has a `## graph-manager` section with the install and start commands, both startup lines, the five flags and the node-pty note.
- [ ] `apps/graph-manager/README.md` leads with the npm way, has the platform table, and no longer says macOS outside Docker or Windows shims are unsupported.
- [ ] `TESTING.md` no longer says the server exits without `GM_PASSWORD`.
- [ ] `docs/wiki/features/npm-manager.md` exists with the four sections and is linked from `docs/wiki/index.md`.
- [ ] The changelog has the Unreleased entry; no `package.json` version changed.
- [ ] Every flag, message and file name in the docs matches the code (check each against the source).
- [ ] No source file under `packages/graph-execution/src` or `apps/graph-manager/src` is changed by this task.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass at the repository root.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
```

Known environment failure, not caused by this task: `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` "exits 2 at startup when --provider claude is not on the PATH" fails wherever a real `claude` is installed next to `node`.
